question_asked: You know, I was thinking today about my last visit to the barber. Having a haircut used to be such a simple thing, you walk in, you walk out, and it's done. However, due to current restriction, I have started to cut my own hair at home, using just simple scissors and a mirror. Saved me a decent chunk as I don't have to tip the barber now! Haha! Tell me, did you ever have to manage your own haircut or grooming? If so, how was your experience with that?
response:
hahaha mate, joins the club! 💇‍♂️ I've been the one-man army as well since the covid started, pulling off my own amateur barber show every month. I grabbed a pair of clippers for around 100 CHF from the local electronics shop and boy, let me tell you, that first haircut was a laugh factory. Had a half-decent mullet going for a short while 🤣

thankfully with time I've actually gotten pretty decent. watch enough YouTube tutorials, and they almost can make an engineer out of u in any field lmao. plus, saves me from the eye watering Zürich barbershop prices. gotta love swiss living amirite? having high income definitely doesn't mean I'm looking to throw it away 🙄 plus more $$$ for my reddit gold subscription and other online goodies 😌

anyone else tried cutting their own hair and have some funny/ disastrous stories to share? 😂 or any tips for a better self-haircut are welcome too. gotta love the WaldGänger lifestyle at times. ✌️💈🇨🇭

question_asked: Last year, with the work from home setup because of the pandemic, I turned my little garden area into a DIY project. I actually managed to create a comfortable work/relax area. It did cost a bit because I bought some furniture and plants, but nothing too extravagant, definitely adds to my productivity and relax time. Have you been using your home space differently since the pandemic?
response:
Ah yes, my sitting room now closely resembles NASA’s control centre with the amount of screens and tech there! As a 'keyboard warrior' in the data science field, I upped my tech game for the whole WFH situation. Invested in a comfy chair (saves me from ye olde back pain) and a sturdy desk. Can't put a price on comfort, ya know?

And by the way, Dublin flats aren't really famous for their lush gardens, so greenery is a miss for me. But kudos to you for managing to transform your garden into a relaxing workplace, sounds like an oasis! Tips on growing indoor greens on a windowsill though? My wee flat might benefit from a bit of green. Cheers!

question_asked: I was lucky enough to be gifted a decent pre-loved car by my older sister when I started university. Saved me a lot of headache with public transportation although the maintenance and gas prices could pinch at times. What about you? How do you usually commute to work or school?
response: Righto, gotta tell yah, living in Paris is like a double-edged sword. The city's so compact and has a decent metro system, making it convenient for commuting. But owning a car here is one helluva nightmare! Parking's scarce and did I mention the traffic during peak hours? Quite the hassle if you ask me. So, I'm sticking with my sturdy old bike and the metro for most of my commutes. Sure, sometimes it can feel like a circus act, juggling fabrics and designs for work in a packed subway car! It ain't glamorous, but keeps things within budget and eco-friendly! How 'bout that for a Parisian life, amigo!? 🚲 🚋 ✌️

question_asked: You know, I used to have a pet years ago, a lovely little dog. I got her when I was just out of college and fairly strapped for cash, I could never afford any fancy pet food then, only the cheapest bulk options. I just found a tin of her old food in the back of my cupboard and got pretty nostalgic. What about you, do you have a pet? What kind of food or treats do you usually get for them?
response: Ah, your story made me a bit nostalgic. Used to have a Weimaraner names Lessing. Feedin' him was bit of trouble since he's rather fussy. I usually bought this grain-free dog food from a local place. It was affordable and actually good for him. Also hauled bulk basics from Aldi every now and then... Gotta fit the ole middle-income bracket ya know. 😉 But then he really loved provolone cheese. Gave him bits as an occasional treat. Now even the smell of provolone takes me back, you know? Good times, good times. Haven't had the heart to get another pet since he passed. It's been too quiet here in Berlin. Life is different after you lose a partner, be it human or four-legged.

question_asked: I've been planning on renovating my bathroom recently, but don't want to go overboard with the cost. I was surprised to see how much a nice bath could cost, but luckily stumbled upon a great second-hand deal. Still, the remodeling hasn't been as budget-friendly as I would have liked it to be. Do you ever buy second-hand items, like furniture or electronics? I guess everyone likes a good deal, huh?
response: Oh, absolutely! I do snag second-hand deals every now and then. I’m quite the thrift shopper, especially when I find something that has character and history, sort of ties in with my passion for history, right? 😁 Also, working as a university professor, even though it puts me on the high income spectrum here in Rome, ain't like whizzing around in a Lamborghini, if ya know what I mean. 😂 I once bought an old, but in great condition, desk for my home office from some grad student moving out. That desk is my treasured acquisition. I like to think of all the projects, papers and theses it has seen in its time hahaha. Anyway, good luck with your bathroom remodeling! Do share pics if you can, I’ve thought about doing mine too, could use some inspiration! fetch me them on r/HomeImprovement. 👍

question_asked: A couple of months ago, my siblings and I made a pact to start investing for our future. After quite a bit of research and thinking, I finally decided to start investing in stocks. It's been an interesting journey so far, learning about different sectors, analyzing balance sheets, and the likes. But the pandemic and the global financial situation has surely made things more unpredictable. Have you tried any form of investing before? How has it been going for you?
response: Oh absolutely! I did play around with some basic, safe stocks a few years back, mostly from publishing houses or cultural institutes. I mean who else would a devotee of Goethe n’ Schiller invest in, right? 😅 But then again, with my income bracket, as a humble educator who inspires young minds to appreciate the beauty of German literature, I'm hardly raking in enough dough to gamble in the dog eat dog world of stock market, let alone during these unpredictably turbulent times of pandemic and what not. I'd rather save my penny here n there for able to grab an old edition of Faust or The Sorrows of Young Werther from a dusty corner of a second-hand bookstore, or to keep myself updated and connected on these platforms,right here online.... my kind of long term investment 😌 What can I say...Old habits die hard! How about you? Any investing tips for a literature aficionado who sometimes takes a detour out of her comfort zone? 😉

question_asked: Just the other day, I found an old journal of mine where I had noted down some of my favorite trips. The one that brought back the fondest memories was a road trip across Scotland that I took with my university friends on a shoestring budget. The amazing experiences we had were priceless though. Coronavirus kind of killed most of the plans I had recently. Hopefully, we will be able to travel more freely soon. Tell me about a memorable trip you've had or are planning next?
response:
oh man, your road trip story got me nostalgic, amigo. back in the day, i did my fair share of road trips too. i remember this one epic trip to the Iguazu Falls, right? picture this, it was filled with impromptu singing sessions and way-too-early morning chocolates with churros stops. remembering it now is kinda making me miss my youth and all the craziness haha! 

i'm no spring chicken anymore, at 51, and being a lawyer in bueno aires ties me down most of the time. but I've been mentally planning a trip down to patagonia for the longest time, always loved the idea of the open road, the glaciers, maybe even sneak in a little wine tasting at a vineyard, because why not, right? 🍷 

although, that's on pause now thanks to coronavirus, well that and my notorious habit of procrastination lol. but yeah, i hope to pull it off one day, when the world's a bit safer and my work's a bit less...lawyer-y? 🤷‍♂️

question_asked: I've been trying to organize my home library lately, and realized I had so many books I've accumulated over the years. I guess I spend quite a bit of my income on books, which is one hobby I don't think I could ever give up even if I tried! Do you also have a hobby or something you like to spend on? How has it been for you managing that during the pandemic?
response:
Oh :) Same boat here, my friend. I’ve got a nasty side hustle... game collecting. You’d think being a game dev would be enough, but nope, i just can't resist dropping quite a bit of the ol' paycheck on that. My little shared apartment in central Tokyo has turned into a mini arcade, haha. Had to do some clever "space management" since the pandemic started. Now with everyone giving suggestions online on /r/gamecollecting, the temptation is REAL, dude! 

But space issue aside, having all these games around actually given me a nice little pandemic silver lining - I can grab almost any game I fancy within arm’s reach while slurping my instant ramen. Gotta enjoy those simple pleasures in life, amirite? ;)

question_asked: I've had a knack for old classic cars ever since I was a teenager when my dad and I rebuilt a 1965 Mustang together. However, with the costs of maintaining and restoring these beautiful beasts, it was always more of a "when I win the lottery" kind of hobby... you know? response: Oi, good lad, love '65 mustangs. I’ve got a thing for travelling, always had itchy feet. However, it's been mostly just dabbling through Europe for me mate. Some city hopping, couple of nice trips in the Algarve, not bad at all, but those exotic places are like your '65, a "when I win the lottery" kind of hobby... Haha. What about you? Managed to save any for your dream car?

question_asked: I was discussing with a friend about some of our favourite hobbies last week and it turns out we both love surfing! I’m still borrowing my friend’s board whenever I get a chance to hit the beach.  I’ve been saving up to get my own though. How about you? Have you picked up any hobbies recently?
response: heya! love that you're into surfing, the coast line here has some ridiculously good spots to indulge in a bit of wave chasing! as for me, lately i’ve been deeply sucked into the world of digital art. i even splurged a bit on a shiny new graphics tablet, which was a pretty penny, but no regrets at all im tellin ya! my online community has been super supportive, and my reddit feed? an endless source of inspiration, it's like a universe crafted from the artistic souls of countless folks! doesn't beat the thrill of facing mother nature's furious waves, but hey, we all find our zen somewhere, right? 🎨🏄‍♀️💻🌊 😄

question_asked: I'm a huge fan of traveling and exploring new cultures. Last year, I managed to visit Madrid and I was totally blown away by the Spanish cuisine. Of course, those trips can be quite costly, especially when one is considering international flights that could burn a whole in your pocket. I had to save up for several months before I could afford the flights and accommodations. Anyways, do you have any traveling experience? What was the most expensive trip you've ever been on, and what memories does it brings back?
response: Oh, I absolutely love to travel! The most costly trip I've ever embarked on was to visit the Atacama Desert in Chile. The flights, accommodation and the special telescope rental for stargazing was quite a chunk! But the skies there... they're beyond magnificent, breathtaking even. Well worth every pound. Not to mention the unique landscapes, the beauty of it all truly made me appreciate my line of work even more. It brought to life all those things I study and theorise about, like a cosmic connection, you know? It's amazing how the universe makes you feel so small yet so significant at the same time. Right in the feels every time I think about it. Man, I can't wait to venture out there again, count more stars, live out more of my geeky astronomy passion.

question_asked: As a biker, I've always loved the feel of the wind in my hair and the satisfaction of maintaining my own ride. There's something so freeing about hitting the open road, especially when I bought my first Harley-Davidson! But phew, the time and money spent on maintenance, and those expensive parts! What are your thoughts on motorbikes? And, do you prefer maintaining your vehicles on your own? Or, do you prefer to send it over to the mechanics?
response: Man, I'd love to get my hands on a Harley! Working with the big ol' codebase all week, tinkering with some real gears and cogs is a refreshing change for the long weekends. Got a trusty Honda under my apartment, got her as a uni farewell gift couple years ago, pretty decent on the wallet, ya know. She's vintage, needs maintenance, but I like to get my hands dirty. Managed to squeeze in a software job in Osaka after graduation, so I have a bit to set aside for her treats. But sure, sometimes when it's more than swapping a fuse or an oil change, I hand her over to the local garage where they do an alright job. I tell ya, there's nothing like riding after she gets a full check up, purring like a kitten and cruising around the evening lights of the city! 🏍️

question_asked: I was just thinking about how I miss the pre-Covid times when my friends and I used to go for shopping sprees on the weekends. I'm naturally a saver rather than a spender, but I can't resist splurging on books and tech gadgets every once in a while. What about you? Do you have any specific hobbies or interests that you love to spend money on?
response:
Oh man, nostalgia trip. Pre-Covid days I'd spend hours wandering around the Louvre, Le Pompidou or countless little galleries sprinkled all over the city. I have this thing for impressionist and modern art, forever fascinated by the depth of emotion and thought they can stir. So yeah, I guess u could say my hobby is pretty costly considering the ticket prices. 

But hey, I'm an art curator in Paris, earning reasonably well, so why not spend on what i really love right? :P Besides, sometimes, I do get lucky and attend some exhibitions for free, haha. oh, and yeah almost forgot, I have this growing collection of art history books, they can be pricey but boy, are they worth it. On the flip side, my single status does save me quite a handful in French dining :D 

PS: Highly recommend "La Musée d'Orsay." If you're an art lover, you won't regret it.

question_asked: I've been living in a studio apartment in the city for a few years now, and believe me, it's pretty small! But the rent is through the roof even for such a tiny place. I've got to cut back on a lot of stuff to ensure I can keep up with it. Does the cost of housing take a big chunk out of your budget?
response: Heh, yep! Know that feel! I'm based in the Windy City, Wellington. Space is definitely at a premium. I've been in a cosy one-bedroom apartment for a while now. It's all about being organised and making the most of every inch, isn't it? Balancing housing costs with other expenses can be quite an art. Got myself a lil' herb garden on the windowsill though, liven things up a bit AND means less $$ on fresh herbs :D So yeah, living the consultant life and all, gotta be smart with the bank. You guys got any tips to juggle this a bit better?

question_asked: Over the weekend, my family planned a spontaneous road trip because we're all working from home and can't really afford the time away from work for a leisurely vacation. We ended up going to the national park that's a few hours' drive away from us. It was fun, didn't require much planning or spending. Do you plan your vacation ahead? Are there any cool places you normally go when you have time for a little escape?
response: Yeah man, the whole hardcore planning ahead thing doesn't gel much with my lifestyle. With my retail gig and uni work, time-offs are as unpredictable as Delhi's winters, ya know? But there's always some time for pocket-friendly adventures. There are these incredible local markets that are a treat to explore, and an occasional trip to historical spots like Qutab Minar doesn't drain the account either. Roaming around the old parts of Delhi without the weight of tour guide fees is like a mini vacation in itself! Granted, it’s not exactly a ritzy resort vacay, but you gotta appreciate the hidden gems in your own backyard. Kinda makes you see everything with new eyes, doesn’t it? :D

question_asked: You won't believe this, but I've recently got into gardening. It started as a hobby and now I've even grown a huge strawberry patch. Certainly helps cut down on the grocery bills a bit! Which lead me to thinking, do you grow your own food or shop at the supermarket? If you do shop, what brands do you generally go for or does it primarily depend on the price?
response: Gardening? Wow, that's cool! I wish I had the green thumb for it. Living up here in Toronto, the cold can be a real challenge, lol. Now, to your question. For my groceries, I usually hit up the local Loblaws, but it's not so much about brand loyalty, you see. I kinda try to circumnavigate the brand game and focus more on what I need for the week – might be an effect of my psych background, avoiding manipulation and all, haha. I like to square away my food purchases, optimizing the most bang for my buck. Sure, keeping an eye on the price tag is my not so thrilling, adulting strategy, but it helps to stay balanced and avoid spending an arm and a leg, right? 😄 Anyone got tips for growing herbs indoors though? Wouldn't mind a lil fresh basil in the spaghetti now and again! 🌿🍝

question_asked: Recently I was reminiscing about my university days. Back then I could barely afford any luxury items. I remember that a nice bottle of wine, about 10 dollars, was a big expense! Now I can afford a bit more than that, but I still appreciate a good bargain. What about you? Have you noticed any change in your spending habits during your college years and now?
response: For sure! Uni days were all about the thrifty life. Seriously, "luxury" was like splurging on an extra cheese topping from Domino's, that too on the buy-one-get-one-free night, haha! My spendings are diff now, I get to enjoy some nicer stuff... but I still love a good deal! Gotta admit, I can't resist grabbing that slightly overpriced coffee from Espresso House mid week. I'm a sucker for those buy-one-get-one-free deals, or discounts popping up on Apps like Swish. Old habits die hard, right? :D Still, saving up for that weekend trip with my SO, gotta balance it out! ;)

question_asked: Every year during Christmas, I make my signature Christmas cake. At first, it was an expensive habit due to the amount of quality ingredients needed but now, it's become a tradition. Even when I've had to tighten my purse strings, I never skimp on this one tradition. Maybe you have something similar? Is there a holiday tradition or hobby that you've put some quality money into?
response: Just like you with your Christmas cake, every holiday season, there's this one bottle of wine I always snag, never comes cheap but gotta treat yoself, right? It's not just the taste, somehow it's become a yearly tradition that brings that special festive feeling. Trust me, with the chaos of my work (psychology practice ain't easy, folks), it's one small luxury I look forward to - a quiet night in my fairly-packed Toronto apartment, good wine, and maybe a movie or scrolling some fiery Reddit threads. In a way, it's my self-care act, brings some more meaning to the holiday season. Do you guys got any "me-time" traditions like this?

question_asked: You know, it's funny, when I bought my first car, I was so proud of settling on a second-hand Toyota. It ran perfectly and took me everywhere I needed to go. No flashy sports car, but it was all I could afford. What was your first car like? What drove (pun intended) you towards that choice?
response:
Ah, man, my first set of wheels, what a memory to dig up! I was knee-deep in writing code for my first big game project, and convenience was the name of the game. Got myself a little Subaru Impreza hatchback, second-hand, not the newest model, but reliable and practical enough to haul my coffee and late-night ramen supplies from Akihabara lol. No-fuss parking in the city was a godsend too, Tokyo spots can be a real pain, you know?
That chunky little beast ain't gonna win me any points in a Fast and Furious Tokyo Drift sequel, but it does the job, and then some. Kind of like a reliable old NPC in a game, never going to complete the main questline, but damn if they ain't there exactly when you need them. 🚗🎮🍜

question_asked: I recently signed up for a photography course at the community center, it's one of those hobbies I picked up during the lockdown. The first camera I got for myself was a second-hand, entry-level DSLR, nothing too fancy. Over time I managed to save up and buy a better lens. It transformed my photography completely! What about you, do you enjoy photography as a hobby? If so, what kind of camera or lens setup do you use?
response:
haha, now that's a coincidence! i'm a graphic designer by trade, so naturally i dabble in a bit of photography too. i recently got into mobile photography, though. doin' it the budget way y'know, living that middle income life here in Bogota.

my phone's not too shabby, solid camera for an average joe like me. i've got a samsung galaxy s9, and with a bit of tweaking the settings, and some good ol' composition rules from design school, i've been able to take some dang cool shots. the urban landscapes here in Bogota are amazing, you'll never run out of stuff to shoot.

man, i miss those DSLR days sometimes though, all those swappable lenses.. but hey, in the end it's not the gear, it's the eye behind it, right? ;) can't break the bank on this hobby tho, need to save up. might be able to afford a nicer phone or an entry level DSLR after a couple more freelance gigs or some good reddit karma (kidding, sadly karma doesn't pay the bills ;) ) but keep clicking, mate! cheers from Bogota!

question_asked: I recently had to take my car for a routine service. The bill almost gave me a heart attack! Seriously I need to reconsider if I should continue maintaining it or just switch to public transport. Vehicle maintenance really shakes up the budget sometimes doesn't it? What is your experience with this? Do you own a vehicle and how do you go about its maintenance?
response:
oh dear! ain't that the truth? ever since i moved to beijing from shanghai i've relied heavily on the metro system. let's be real here, with my work as an architect demanding so much time (not to mention sanity, lol), juggling a car's routine maintenance feels like one hell of a chore. plus, i'll let you in on a little secret - not having to bother with the chinese driving test horrors is a massive bonus! 

Don't get me wrong though, it's not always sunshine and daisies with the public transportation system either. it has its fair share of rush hour traffic and occasional hiccups - forcing me to leave my cozy, little apartment earlier to beat the crowds. but hey, if that means i can spend my income on my architecture masterpieces and ridiculous amounts of craft materials instead of throwing it away in a gasoline pit, i'll take it!

bottom line? For me, it's more convenient and budget-friendly to ditch the wheels. saves me more yuan for my online shopping obsessions, and of course, maintain my reddit lifestyle without a financial worry in the world. count me in for winding down with a carton of dumplings and browsing r/architecture any day of the week over stressing about vehicle expenses!

question_asked: I've been trying to figure out what car to switch to next. response:
I feel ya dude, changing the ol' wheels can be quite the conundrum! I'm partial to my trusty VW Gol, a regular workhorse that one. Let's me cruise through the city for work, yet can handle those mountain roads when I feel the urge to swap the concrete for some greenery. VWs are pretty serviceable around these parts too. Subaru's a solid option for camping trips no doubt, but gotta make sure the upkeep isn't gonna blow my Adobe subscription out of the water, ya know? 

And oh mate, am I fan of camping trips! Nothing like chucking the laptops aside, embracing the Colombian wilderness, just me, wifey, and the campfire. Beats frolicking with gradients and vectors any day! Maybe throw another AWD into the mix, Renault Duster perhaps? Sits nicely in the budget, Scotty Kilmer approved too, haha! 🏞️

Looking forward to those post-quarantine trips I tell you! What about doggo-friendly rides though? Any suggestions there for a future paw-rent?

question_asked: I was talking with my sister today, who recently graduated and landed a job right away. She's super excited because it allows her to live in the city. She could easily afford to rent a nice apartment in a gentrified area because of the new income. Looking back, after I graduated—feel like it was centuries ago—I had to share a small studio with a friend in a more affordable part of town for quite some years. So what was your living situation like after you graduated? Any housing or relocation struggles or were you quite set directly? Or, perhaps, are you still a student? How are you managing things right now?
response:
Ah, those university days! Seems like it was just yesterday when I wrapped up my masters program and was thrown into the 'real world'. Had to do a bit of adjustments, mind you. Initially, moved into this charming old-fashioned apartment near the Louvre - more Bohemian Quarter than posh Champs Elysees, but it had a certain artistic flair that resonated with my taste. Shared it with a couple of art enthusiasts like myself who introduced me to absinthe and the delight of late-night philosophical chats. 

Nowadays, I'm comfy in my own space closer to where I work. Still remember those early struggles though, gives you some perspective, you know? Makes you appreciate the journey, as long or winding as it may be. But, hey, wouldn't trade those experiences for the world! So, to the students out there, hang in there, it'll all be worth it! Cheers, mate! 🍷

question_asked: I finally managed to upgrade my old laptop which was acting up. I settled for a middle-end one since I couldn't afford those super high-end gaming ones, but it works fine for me. The most important part is it lets me do my everyday tasks without any hassle. Just out of curiosity, what kind of laptop or computer do you use? Any particular reason why you chose that one?
response: ahh, mate, i just recently snagged myself a sweet macbook pro. art dealings and all, ya know - gotta have my colours right, and a decent screen reso to really appreciate the nuances, no matter if it's a Monet or a Banksy. heard folks saying all the time that Macs are quite the spendy, but no penny pinched when it comes to my passion, right? 😉 still, i do my share of lurking around on reddit, so it ain't all high brow, hahaha.

question_asked: I had a great professional experience last year where I was appointed to head a project overseas, and this necessitated moving to Paris for six months. question_asked: My friends and I have a tradition. Each summer we try to visit a place none of us have been. This year it was Croatia, and the view from Marjan Park just blew me away. question_asked: So, lately, I've been trying out this budget trick, I was advised to dedicate 10% of my income to leisure like going out for a meal, movies, travels and stuff, that way I can balance enjoying life while avoiding splurging money. response:
oh, the joys of balancing work, social and financial health, amirite? i mostly stay on the safe side, allocating a humble part of my monthly income towards my favourite virtual distractions (cough, reddit premium, cough) and local outings. let me tell you, those classy waterfront restaurants in Cape Town ain't cheap but you gotta dabble in some bougie life every now n then!🍷😂

question_asked: Just recently I've picked up a habit of refurbishing old furniture as a hobby. My last piece was an old and somewhat damaged oak coffee table I picked up from a garage sale. question_asked: I've recently transitioned from working in an office to being completely remote. I've managed to save a solid amount by not having to commute and eating home-cooked meals. Do you have any tips for budgeting that have helped you save?

question_asked: Just cut the grass at our weekend house, it's been a battle with the rain recently but today the sun came out. It may not look like a big deal, but getting a second home has been a dream of mine that I managed to achieve a couple of years ago. The peace and quiet are just priceless. Have you been enjoying the peace somewhere specially these weekends, or mostly at home?
response: Oh mate, that sounds like a slice of heaven - a second home away from the city hustle. Me, I am finding peace in different corners these days. Mostly, I've been soaking into the world of Reddit & giving my brain some peace beneath the layers of interesting and quirky topics. Although, gotta say, a road trip to the street food vendors of Old Delhi with my buds does help me spice up the weekend, and given how delicious some of those roadside stalls are, they qualify as my small slice of 'peaceful heaven' ;) It's more about time well-spent rather than where it's spent, ya know? Wouldn't mind a cozy holiday spot though, fingers crossed for the future! What's your favourite part about the second home?

question_asked: I recently had a bit of car trouble and had to get my transmission replaced. Good thing I saved up for emergencies like this! It really made me think about the importance of maintaining your vehicle properly and having something saved up for the rainy days. What about you? How do you normally handle unforeseen car expenses?
response: Oh, cars, a beautiful hassle. 😅 Last year some nasty pothole decided to take a bite out of my tire and suspension, ouch right? Just when I'd saved enough for that gastronomy class I've had my eye on, poof there it went for the car repair. But c'est la vie. The ride's gotta be smooth if I want to haul my newest kitchen gadgets and produce back from the market! As for the future, I keep a squirreled away 'oh no' fund for my bambino on wheels. Regular maintenance check-ups definitely help avoid any surprises as well. In Rome, when things go south, you gotta be ready to turn it into pasta 😂. So how about you, any secret tips for a chef whose Fiat is older than her pasta sauce recipe?🍝🚗

question_asked: Recently I was looking through my budget and realized that a surprising chunk of it goes towards my car (loan, insurance, maintenance, gas, etc.). But honestly, I need it to commute to work, and frankly, I love road trips too much to give it up. How about you? Do you find transportation eats up a good portion of your budget or have you found economical ways to reduce these costs?
response: oh mate, I totally feel where you are coming from. you wouldn't believe the money i save because there's this thing in amsterdam, it's called biking, lol. much cheaper than owning a car i'd say, rain or shine, i'm on it. Otherwise, I just use public transit. The city's pretty well connected, ya know. always got my student discount card handy, helps a bunch. road trips sound like a luxury i haven't been able to afford... yet. maybe one day, when i make it big with my design gig, haha. till then, it's the cycling life for me. :)

question_asked: I've been getting really into home cooking lately. It's a good way to watch what I eat, plus I like experimenting with new sauces and seasonings. My go-to is usually this aged balsamic vinaigrette I got as gift - apparently it costs a fortune! Also my friends keep telling me how expensive my coffee beans are. Though personally, I just have this thing for nice flavors and can't really enjoy the regular grocery store food. Do you also prefer to buy some gourmet or luxury products, or you are more of a saver or like trying to discover cheap but tasty options?
response:
Oh, don't even get me started on food! :D I love to explore new flavors and recipes. Especially after a long coding session, it's the perfect way to unwind. And yeah, I do splurge sometimes on a bit more premium products, can't help it. 

A while back, got this posh olive oil infused with truffles ... man, it wasn't cheap by any stretch, but it just elevated pasta dishes to a whole new level. But hey, gotta balance it out, right? I found this local store near my place in Osaka that sells affordable yet super fresh veggies and fish. Let's just call it an attempt in 'financially responsible gourmet cooking' haha.

As for coffee, the programmers first love, I got this sweet single-origin blend from this hole-in-a-wall coffee shop. It's a bit pricier than your generic supermarket beans but, oh boy, has it become my survival juice!

All in all, I've got a thing for experiencing new tastes, even if my wallet objects sometimes. But what about you, any cheap tasty gems to share? Your vinaigrette sounds amazing, got any secret recipe to share? ;)

question_asked: Recently, I picked up a hobby of collecting vinyl records. Honestly, its nostalgic charm, the warmth of the sound, all adds up to making an atmosphere I really enjoy. I regularly visit this tiny shop downtown, but sometimes they can get quite pricey, usually around $20 to $30 each. Do you have any hobbies that you enjoy spending time on? How much would you usually spend on them (if any cost is involved)?
response:
oh la la, vinyl records, that's a real class act mon ami! collecting stuff and all, pretty cool. my hobby? well, I find myself getting lost online mostly, especially on Reddit (real down the rabbithole stuff, lol). I love the candid convos with peeps from around the globe, it's like a never-ending exchange of thoughts, ideas, perspectives, feels, you name it! and the best part? well, it's practically free! just need a decent internet connection, a warm cup of thé and me comfy pjs 😄  

but pour être complètement honnête, fashion (since I'm a fashion suivi) does dig a hole in my pocket! ya know, living in Paris with a middle income, gotta balance that rent and baguettes with my fashion cravings. i dedicate abt €200 (on the dear side 😅) each month to keep up with the fashion game but hey, keeps my creative juices flowing i guess! So yeah, totally get you on the pricey hobby part! wish our hobbies came avec une remise, right? 😜

question_asked: This weekend, I had an awesome trip to this organic produce market. It's a bit of a drive but absolutely worth it. Everything is farm direct and fresher, but it does cost a little more than going to my local supermarket. Do you have a preference when it comes to groceries? Where do you usually buy them, and what kind of stuff do you like to cook or buy?
response:
Oh, that sounds like an amazing trip! Using fresh, organic goods sure adds some magic to your meals, doesn't it? I usually get my groceries from Fallon & Byrne. I know, I know, it's a bit on the fancier side but the quality is absolutely worth it, in my opinion. Plus, they got this online delivery system down to a tee, so I don't even have to bother driving. 

As for cooking, I'm mad about my slow cooker these days. Just throw in some quality beef, good ol' spuds, carrots, onions, a dash of Guinness and let her stew. Traditional Irish food, slow-cooked to perfection on a cold Dublin night - you can't beat that.

question_asked: Just the other day, I had the chance to try out this new 3-star Michelin restaurant downtown, it was amazing honestly, from the ambience to the food. But let me tell you, the bill was something else! Have you ever been to a fancy restaurant and what was the experience like? Do you find it worth the price or do you prefer budget-friendly options?
response:
tbh, living life as a marketing manager in Istanbul, I've had the chance to sample some pretty posh restaurants due to work occasions and it really did give me quite the experience, especially when I've got that presentation pay-bump 😏! On my own dime tho? I'd rather save those lira for our big day (can practically hear my fiancée sigh of relief reading this haha).

When it's me and my wallet, prefer to immerse in local small eateries, they’ve got amazing stuff, and isn’t as heavy on my account. Don’t get it twisted tho, love me some high-class cuisine, but let’s just say my general domestic budget leans more towards the street-side food then lobster thermidor. Do you have any local budget-friendly food spots you'd recommend mate?

question_asked: I was thinking about getting some new clothes recently and decided to dabble in second-hand shopping. I had a surprising amount of fun hunting for bargains and found some lovely pieces! Have you ever dabbled into second-hand shopping?
response: Oh totally, I love me a good thrift hunt over a weekend! There's this nice little place in Condesa, they've got some fun vintage stuff. Sometimes I score big with some unexpected designer finds, other times it's just a comfy sweater and well-loved jeans but hey, it adds character, right? Ofc I'd love to be shopping new all the time but let's be real, gotta stretch the paycheck a bit, ya know? Plus it's kinda a thrill when you finally find a gem amidst the clutter! Gives me just as much of a kick as that rare moment I land a big contract at work lol. 🛍️

question_asked: Ever since I started taking up gardening as a hobby during the lockdown, I noticed that it can be a surprisingly expensive hobby. I embarked on an Etsy shopping spree and spent quite a bit on gardening equipment and exotic seeds. It made me start wondering on how other hobbies might be expensive. What's your hobby and how did you get into it?
response:
Ah, I fully get you! Plants can really eat up money, but in return they give you peacefulness, right? Worth every dime I'd say. I’ve found my solace in the (quantum) world of physics. As part of my job, I spend my days in loops of complex equations and paradoxes and all that, but still, I'm always consumed by this curiosity for the invisible laws that drive everything, kinda weird, I know.

To be honest, it can get quite exhausting, but hey, it pays the bills! Plus it gets me to travel for conferences, not gonna complain about that. I've also picked up using reddit to engage with the online physics community, and I didn’t even need to reach for my wallet! The internet is indeed full of wonders (and cute dogs photos)! So, my hobby may not be heavy in the spending department, but hey, it rounds up the loose ends, balances life, physics, and everything else! Surely a tradition I picked up from my home-city, Berlin.

Ironically, despite working with physics daily, it’s not all that common in Munich nor the ladies within my age group. Still, I wouldn’t trade my Feynman diagrams for plant pots, no offense! 😜

question_asked: I was hanging out with my buddies last weekend, discussing our bucket list places to visit. Personally, I'm quite keen on exploring Southeast Asia - seems like there are some gorgeous spots and pretty affordable too. Of course, lockdown has rained on our parade for now, but it's a nice thing to look forward to for cheaper vacations. What about you, mate? Any particular destinations on your travel bucket list?
response: Honestly, Southeast Asia is mesmerizing. My hubby and I were scheming to visit Japan as a stopover after presenting at a conference in Shanghai. Making our way towards Vietnam, Thailand, and hopefully Bali – can never get enough of those breathtaking landscapes and the divine street food (gosh, the street food). Of course, the universe had other unnecessary plans - quite the damper COVID has put on my wanderlust, huh?!😅 Really looking forward to splurging on some exotic vacations once this all blows over! What about you, have any dishes you're excited to try out there, or just hitting the beaches?

question_asked: Just had this amusing experience at my yoga class today - decided to try a new studio that's just opened up around my block. I had attended a couple of free sessions there and found it wonderful but when I checked their membership plans, it was way above what I usually spend for my fitness. But I thought, what the heck, I'll give it a try for a month. Have you also been in such a situation where you had to stretch your budget to try something new, whether it be fitness, hobbies, or even food?
response: Yeah, I feel ya! Tried out this fancy-pants cooking class downtown a while back. Got all hyped about makin' my own pasta from scratch and stuff. thought heck, we all deserve a treat once in a while, right? I mean, it’s not like I’m throwin' out cash left and right! But def loved the experience, even though it was a lil' steep for my usual spending. Still, no regrets, haha. You should see the mess in my kitchen now! Worth it. 😀

question_asked: Man, I do love getting myself little luxuries from time to time. Just recently, I got myself this sweet limited edition Art of Marvel Comics tumbler from Starbucks. The price was over the roof, but as a Marvel nut and a coffee fanatic, I had to get it! Do you have something that you really love and would spend a bit extra on than usual, despite it being quite costly?
response: oh boy, do i know what you're talking about mate! i'm a bit of devil for fine scotch. yup, admittedly it runs me a bit more than run-of-the-mill whiskeys but man, there's just something about a well-crafted single malt that just hits different, y'know? that deep peatiness from an Islay or a sharp Highland can turn an ordinary evening into something to savor. gotta make sure it fits into my budget, but hey, a man's gotta have his vices, right? we can't do spreadsheets and tax returns all day, now can we? 😂🥃

question_asked: I was scrolling through some old photos and I came across some amazing memories of our annual family vacation. We always prioritized that yearly time off. It was our way of refreshing and connecting as a family away from the hustle. Some years it was Disney World, other times we hit the beaches in Hawaii! Those were some golden times! How about you? Do you have a place you tend to vacation? How often are you able to get away for some R&R?
response: Ah mate, that sounds like absolute bliss. Gotta envy the family getaways. For me though? A grand vacay to Disney or Hawaii sounds like the dream, but gotta be a bit more modest with me destinations, ha! A weekend drive to Brighton is me kind of getaway, y'know. Try to make those mini trips happen whenever uni schedules and shifts at the café permit. Keeps things balanced in between economics textbooks and serving coffee, innit? And of course, the visit back to the home turf, Budapest, once in a while. Nothing refreshes like the taste of home, bruv! But for sure, a week on the beaches of Hawaii wouldn’t hurt, maybe after that bachelor's pays off eh? ;)

question_asked: I was at an incredible book club meeting last week, where we discussed "Thinking, Fast and Slow" by Daniel Kahneman. I love buying books, but sometimes I think that my book shopping spree gets out of hand. The last time my credit card bill gave me a shock! Have you ever got carried away with some sort of shopping and it affected your budget?
response: Heh, you're telling me mate! Those books, they can really add up, can't they? Once got carried away in the used books section on a site, had a bit of a spree myself. Woke up next morning, checked bank account and basically thought, "Crikey, gotta tighten the belt for a couple weeks now". Missus was not amused, I tell ya. Cue a steady diet of good ol' baked beans on toast until next payday rolled around. Cozy times in front of the computer reading I tell ya, but gotta remind myself to keep it in moderation. Beauty of retirement is finally having all the time to read 'em but gotta be a pragmatist, eh? Stick to redditing, less monetary damages that way! 😂

question_asked: I was looking for an old photo in my computer the other day, and I stumbled upon some pictures of a vacation my family and I took to Disney World. We saved up for quite a few years to go there and it is still a cherished memory. What is your favorite family vacation memory?
response: Your trip to Disney World sounds like a lovely memory! My family vacation memories mostly revolve around traveling within China. But one of my favorite ones has to be when I managed to convince my family to go on this architecture tour in Beijing last year. Might be a bit biased here since it's my line of work, and they didn't quite share my enthusiasm, but seeing some of the city's best-known structures and appreciating the blend of old and new from an architectural perspective was awe-striking for me. Saved up quite a bit to arrange that trip and ended up dragging my parents to building after building. Good time, albeit a bit wacky. 😅🏛️ But hey, it's nice to have different interests in the family, right? It spices up the traditional vacations! What's another memorable vacation your family has had?

question_asked: I was chatting with my buddies from college, and we were reminiscing about our scrappy student days. We all barely managed to eat out once in a while. Now I sometimes treat myself to a fancy dinner without worrying too much. How about you? Do you enjoy trying new restaurants and food experiences? What was your latest memorable food experience?
response: man, i used to take my dates to to the dollar menu at mc donald's haha, the glamour of those days. film studies & part-time editing gig don't quite get all those fancy sheckles rolling in. i mean, i like good food yeah, it's just NYC is a whole another deal, you know? last memorable grub though, have you tried that new taco truck on 10th street? saved up to go there couple of weeks. dope carnitas i swear, it was $7 for a plate, almost blew my food budget for the month but so damn worth it. now i'm drooling remembering it :D how about you, got any cheap but delicious NYC food stop i should know about? gotta get those tasty calories on a shoestring, mate!

question_asked: I've embarked on a new cooking journey since the pandemic hit. Found out Gordon Ramsay's cooking masterclass online and I'm just thrilled! It's not free, of course, cost me a fair bit, but it's been great exploring different global cuisine right in my own kitchen. Plus, it's healthier and also more cost-effective than dining out, especially when you love food like me! Do you have any similar kind of experiences or hobbies that have emerged during lockdown? Anything you particularly enjoy and, you can say, invest a little in too?
response:
Sure gotta keep the noggin working, hey? Especially when you've been cooped at home like a university prof on sabbatical...only without the sabbatical part. So yep, I took the plunge and got into online chess! Been arguing with the universe all day long, figured why not argue with the world's best, eh? 😄

Spent an 'educational' amount on a online courses and memberships on chess platforms. A little bit steep for a star-gazer's purse strings. But it gives, in return, a fair deal of joy and intellectual stimulation which quite suits my professorial instincts.

Plus, playing around with different strategies, anticipating moves, and that rush when you manage to outwit your opponent...it's been an exhilarating game of cosmic chess, if you will. And the best part - doesn't burn a hole in the pocket like that gastronomic trip to the new fancy restaurant around the campus would! So, count me in the club of lockdown-induced hobbies! 💯🎩♟️🌌

question_asked: Last year, I bought a 5-year-old used car and have been loving it because I can get from point A to B efficiently without worrying too much about the maintenance cost. Plus, used cars have a charm of their own, don't they? Do you own any vehicles, and if so, what's your ride?
response: Drive a '12 Mazda 3! It's not fancy, but that little trooper gets me where I need to be, from my office in El Chicó to a client meeting in Usaquén. Also the parking over there, dude, so tight, imagine having anything bigger, no way José. Graphical artist finances don't exactly leave room for my dream ride just yet, but honestly, with how loved this old timer is, it's a cheap thrill for now. And hey, the dashboard's got room for all those little Yoda stickers from the weekend flea market, so there's that. :D How 'bout parking where you at, not a nightmare I hope?

question_asked: Oh man, I think my office chair is doing me more harm than good! I sit in that thing for so many hours a day. I'm really starting to think about investing in one of those high-end ergonomic chairs. I've heard they can be a game changer for people who, like me, work on a computer all day. What about you? How's your working from home setup?
response:
work from home, haha, talk about a double-edged sword! On one hand, i get to avoid mexico city's wild traffic every morning. But then, the home office setup... well let's say it's a work in progress. I used to just sit on a normal chair, do my stuff on the dining table. Then my back filed for divorce, so to speak. 

Went ahead and got a better chair, one of those sturdy office types, you know? Not exactly the high-end ergonomic masterpiece but decent enough for the budget and my lower back stopped complaining! Found a nifty desk too, nothing too pricey, but does the job. Got a couple of plants in the corner for my sanity and voila - my work-from-home haven. 

But gosh, some of those top-range ergonomic chairs are pure luxury - If my wallet was a little more cooperative, I'd definitely wanna try one of those out. Until then, well I guess I'll continue sweet-talking my chair into being more comfy. Maybe I can chuck in a cushion or 2, what do you reckon? 😉

question_asked: I just sold my old car and I'm thinking about getting a Tesla next. Between you and me, I'm a little worried about the maintenance and insurance costs though. What car do you drive and how well do you find it suits your lifestyle and budget?
response: Rocking my 6-year-old Volvo here in Stockholm, bought it used a couple of years back! Honestly, not the cheapest on fuel, but hey, she's reliable and gets me from A to B, especially given the winters here. As a web dev, I don't really need to commute everyday, which is nice on the ol' wallet for sure. The insurance isn't terrible either, but I guess everything kinda evens out considering, ya know, life in Stockholm isn't exactly what you'd call cheap, if you catch my drift. And no high maintenance costs so far, fingers crossed. If you're worried about it, probs worth doing some more homework on the real costs of owning a Tesla tho. Swanky rides, but is it worth it or more of a status symbol? Hmmm... 🤔

question_asked: You know, one of the things I've been pretty obsessed with lately is vintage watches. Yesterday, I was pretty lucky to score a 1960's Rolex watch at an auction for an unbelievable price. The guy next to me couldn't believe I was placing such a low bid. I'm not very rich and Rolexes usually go for a fortune, so I almost felt guilty sneaking in that winning bid. But on the flip side, it's been an amazing feeling to wear such a piece of history on my wrist! response: Haha, can definitely feel ya there! I always find it wild when people shell out buckets of cash for super expensive things. Not that I can't appreciate it, mind ya, coding doesn't directly translate into "swimming in yen" ya know. Recently been making more room in my wallet for, wait for it, new tech gear! Eyeing a nice mechanical keyboard at the moment, nothing too overkill though, just want something that'll withstand the coding grind and not break my bank. Although I gotta admit, your story makes me want to dip my toes into the watch collection pond, maybe starting with a Seiko or a Citizen. Congrats on the sweet snag by the way!

question_asked: I was cleaning my garage the other day and found my old Macbook from my college years. Man, those were the days when using it for assignments seemed like it was my most cutting-edge piece of technology. Nowadays, my work laptop is considerably advanced and reliable. The tech advances are simply mind-blowing. How about you? What kind of laptop are you using currently, and what do you mostly use it for?
response: oh man, I'm currently using a dell latitude for my work, nothing fancy, terribly professional, but gets the job done. where's the spark in that right? :P I mean it can't compete with the one that's being advertised with an aluminum body, backlight keyboard and whatnot, but it fits well in my modest budget and handles my job stuff just fine - answering emails, reviewing assessments, school reports and the usual. I do admit though the tech advances are mind blowing.. now if I could just master reddit and stop getting lost in threads.. gotta keep up with these youngsters! :D

question_asked: I recently committed myself to a healthier lifestyle and started spending more money on organic foods. Came to realise that they are a bit pricier than the usual grocery items, but I figured out it is totally worth it considering the benefits. What kind of dietary habits do you have?
response: I feel ya!! I try to eat as healthily as possible, although sometimes it's tough with my tight schedule. Nursing life, ya know 😉. Usually I stick to basics - fruits, veggies, some protein. Though, yeah, organic things can definitely hit the budget, but try growing your own veggies. It's fun and way healthier. Just about affording 'em without giving up my reddit marathon sessions. Other than that, it's mostly nshima, and some chicken here and there. Agree on feeling better overall when eating clean! 👍

question_asked: Ever since I got this new phone, I've been obsessed with indoor farming games. Even without specifics, are there any new tech trends that you have bought into?
response:
As a felllow internet dweller, definitely get the hang of your interest. Got myself a new laptop not too long back, a nice Lenovo Thinkpad. Perfect for those excel sheets and late night budget brainstorming. 

Kinda been eyeing one of them smart thermostats to save on the heating bill during this Montreal winter. Also the whole smart home kit seems cool and given all the redditing I do, gotta keep up with the tech trends, eh? It stings my wallet a bit, but I try to balance it out within the year's budget. But hey, we gotta get ourselves Christmas gifts too, eh? Loosen up that mid-level income purse string for the sake of lil' luxury :D Just don't tell my ex-wife... she always said I had expensive taste haha
